premise.claim: When a RoleBasedGroupSet / RoleBasedGroup is deleted and recreated with the same name, the new object gets a new UID while the predecessor's children linger until GC: the recreated Set listed children purely by the set-name label (could delete a foreign child on scale-down, rewrite its spec, count it Ready in status); the RBG controller read a bound ScalingAdapter by name (a leftover adapter could pin a stale replica count); both gang PodGroup implementations reused the PodGroup found by name and rewrote its spec while keeping the old controller reference, and the Volcano path never adopted orphans.
premise.reportedComponent: RoleBasedGroupSet controller, RoleBasedGroup controller (scaling-adapter paths), pkg/scheduler/k8s-scheduler-plugin, pkg/scheduler/volcano
premise.evidence: All five P0 contract tests FAIL on base 56c4953 (foreign child deleted on scale-down; ReadyReplicas counted 1; role replicas 3 pinned to 9; both foreign PodGroup specs rewritten 1->2 with no error) and PASS on head d2915172. findings._note: Regression suite for the PR's own fix (the P0 tests re-run on every future head). Must keep passing; a flip means the ownership fix regressed.

FIXED on head 4f32bb9f (round 2): the author added '!metav1.IsControlledBy(podGroup, rbg) ||' to the update condition in both schedulers (the exact one-line fix validated in round 1's harness-bites check), plus same-spec orphan test rows in both scheduler suites (TestCreateOrUpdateSameSpecOrphanPodGroupAdopted). Both F1 contract tests now pass on 4f32bb9f; kept as the regression suite against re-breakage.

FIXED on head 4f32bb9f (round 2): ReconcileScalingAdapter's replace-delete now carries the observed adapter UID as a DeleteOptions precondition (internal/controller/workloads/rolebasedgroup_controller.go), with the PR's own TestReconcileScalingAdapter_RecreateUsesUIDPrecondition. This harness test (added round 2) was red on d2915172 and green on 4f32bb9f; kept as the regression suite. Note: the sibling delete in the same function (scaling disabled path, r.client.Delete without preconditions) is still unconditional — tracked as an advisory note in the round-2 findings, not a blocker.
